passages.text: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites heard the bad report about the land.
The whole congregation gathered together.
All the people raised their voices.
They cried out loudly.
That night, the people wept.
passages.original: וַתִּשָּׂא֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ אֶת־ קוֹלָ֑ם וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ הָעָ֖ם בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!
passages.sermon:
All the Israelites spoke against Moses and Aaron.
The Israelites complained.
The whole congregation spoke to Moses and Aaron.
They said, “We wish we had died in Egypt.
We wish we had died in this wilderness.”
passages.original: וַיִּלֹּ֙נוּ֙ עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן כֹּ֖ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֲלֵהֶ֜ם כָּל־ הָעֵדָ֗ה לוּ־ מַ֙תְנוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם א֛וֹ בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לוּ־ מָֽתְנוּ׃

passages.text: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke to Moses and Aaron.
They questioned God’s actions.
They said, “Why is the LORD bringing us into this land?”
They feared they would die by the sword.
They said, “Our wives and children will become plunder.”
They asked, “Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
passages.original: וְלָמָ֣ה יְ֠הוָה מֵבִ֨יא אֹתָ֜נוּ אֶל־ הָאָ֤רֶץ הַזֹּאת֙ לִנְפֹּ֣ל בַּחֶ֔רֶב נָשֵׁ֥ינוּ וְטַפֵּ֖נוּ יִהְי֣וּ לָבַ֑ז הֲל֧וֹא ט֦וֹב לָ֖נוּ שׁ֥וּב מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

passages.text: So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were in the wilderness.
\r\nThey were afraid and unhappy.
\r\nThey spoke to each other.
\r\nThey said, "Let us choose a leader."
\r\nThey said, "Let us go back to Egypt."
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִ֑יו נִתְּנָ֥ה רֹ֖אשׁ וְנָשׁ֥וּבָה מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

passages.text: Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Aaron was his brother and helper.
The Israelites were gathered together.
Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
They did this in front of all the people of Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאַהֲרֹ֖ן עַל־ פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם לִפְנֵ֕י כָּל־ קְהַ֥ל עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the son of Nun.
Caleb was the son of Jephunneh.
Joshua and Caleb were among the men who spied out the land.
Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes.
Joshua and Caleb spoke to the whole congregation of Israel.
They said, “The land we passed through and explored is very, very good.”
passages.original: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־ נ֗וּן וְכָלֵב֙ בֶּן־ יְפֻנֶּ֔ה מִן־ הַתָּרִ֖ים אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ קָרְע֖וּ בִּגְדֵיהֶֽם׃ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֶל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֤רְנוּ בָהּ֙ לָת֣וּר אֹתָ֔הּ טוֹבָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has power.
If the LORD is pleased with us, He will act.
He will bring us into this land.
He will give this land to us.
This land flows with milk and honey.
This land is very good.
passages.original: אִם־ חָפֵ֥ץ בָּ֙נוּ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְהֵבִ֤יא אֹתָ֙נוּ֙ אֶל־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָ֑נוּ אֶ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ הִ֛וא זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”
passages.sermon:
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh spoke to the Israelites.
They said, “Do not rebel against the LORD.
Do not be afraid of the people who live in the land.
The people of the land will be like bread for us.
Their protection is gone.
The LORD is with us.
Do not be afraid of them.”
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ בַּֽיהוָה֮ אַל־ תִּמְרֹדוּ֒ וְאַתֶּ֗ם אַל־ תִּֽירְאוּ֙ אֶת־ עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י לַחְמֵ֖נוּ הֵ֑ם סָ֣ר צִלָּ֧ם מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֛ם וַֽיהוָ֥ה אִתָּ֖נוּ אַל־ תִּירָאֻֽם׃

passages.text: But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites formed a large group called the congregation.
Joshua and Caleb spoke to the congregation.
The congregation became angry at Joshua and Caleb.
The congregation wanted to kill Joshua and Caleb with stones.
The LORD is God.
The LORD’s glory appeared.
The LORD’s glory appeared at the Tent of Meeting.
All the Israelites saw the LORD’s glory.
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לִרְגּ֥וֹם אֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וּכְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֗ה נִרְאָה֙ בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד אֶֽל־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD asked a question about the Israelites.
The LORD said, “How long will these people treat Me with contempt?”
The LORD said, “How long will they refuse to believe in Me?”
The LORD reminded Moses about the signs He performed among the Israelites.
The LORD said, “I have done many signs among them.”
The LORD said, “Still, they do not believe in Me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה עַד־ אָ֥נָה יְנַאֲצֻ֖נִי הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה וְעַד־ אָ֙נָה֙ לֹא־ יַאֲמִ֣ינוּ בִ֔י בְּכֹל֙ הָֽאֹת֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I will strike them with a plague and destroy them—and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God said He would punish the people.
God said, “I will strike the people with a plague.
I will destroy them.
I will make you, Moses, into a nation.
Your nation will be greater than their nation.
Your nation will be mightier than their nation.”
passages.original: אַכֶּ֥נּוּ בַדֶּ֖בֶר וְאוֹרִשֶׁ֑נּוּ וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֹֽתְךָ֔ לְגוֹי־ גָּד֥וֹל וְעָצ֖וּם מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: But Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses said, “The Egyptians will hear about this.
You, LORD, brought this people out from among the Egyptians.
You did this with Your strength.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּֽי־ הֶעֱלִ֧יתָ בְכֹחֲךָ֛ אֶת־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה מִקִּרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
passages.sermon:
The people will speak to the inhabitants of this land.
The inhabitants have already heard about You, LORD.
You, LORD, are present among this people.
You, LORD, have appeared to them face to face.
Your cloud stands over them.
You go before them in a pillar of cloud during the day.
You go before them in a pillar of fire at night.
passages.original: וְאָמְר֗וּ אֶל־ יוֹשֵׁב֮ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּאת֒ שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה בְּקֶ֖רֶב הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־ עַ֨יִן בְּעַ֜יִן נִרְאָ֣ה׀ אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַעֲנָֽנְךָ֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עֲלֵהֶ֔ם וּבְעַמֻּ֣ד עָנָ֗ן אַתָּ֨ה הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבְעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ לָֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say, ‘Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses referred to the Israelites, whom God brought out of Egypt.
Moses said, "If You kill all these people at once, as if they were one man, then the nations will hear about it."
These nations have already heard about Your fame, LORD.
They will say, 'The LORD was not able to bring this people into the land He promised them.'
They will say, 'So He killed them in the wilderness.'
passages.original: וְהֵמַתָּ֛ה אֶת־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁמְע֥וּ אֶֽת־ שִׁמְעֲךָ֖ לֵאמֹֽר׃ מִבִּלְתִּ֞י יְכֹ֣לֶת יְהוָ֗ה לְהָבִיא֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ נִשְׁבַּ֣ע לָהֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: So now I pray, may the power of my Lord be magnified, just as You have declared: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is slow to anger.
The LORD is full of loving devotion.
The LORD forgives iniquity and transgression.
The LORD does not leave the guilty unpunished.
The LORD visits the iniquity of the fathers upon their children.
He does this to the third and fourth generation.
Now, Lord, show Your power.
Do this as You have spoken.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֕ה יִגְדַּל־ נָ֖א כֹּ֣חַ אֲדֹנָ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ יְהוָ֗ה אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֙יִם֙ וְרַב־ חֶ֔סֶד נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֖ן וָפָ֑שַׁע וְנַקֵּה֙ לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֔ה פֹּקֵ֞ד עֲוֺ֤ן אָבוֹת֙ עַל־ בָּנִ֔ים עַל־ שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־ רִבֵּעִֽים׃

passages.text: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to God.
Moses asked God to forgive the sin of the people of Israel.
Moses asked God to forgive them because of His great loving devotion.
Moses reminded God that He has forgiven the people since they left Egypt.
Moses asked God to continue to show mercy to the people.
passages.original: סְלַֽח־ נָ֗א לַעֲוֺ֛ן הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כְּגֹ֣דֶל חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתָה֙ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־ הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke.\r\nThe LORD said, “I have pardoned them.\r\nI have pardoned them as you requested.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה סָלַ֖חְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: “Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD, not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness—yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times— not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD lives forever.
The LORD fills the whole earth with His glory.
Many men saw the LORD’s glory.
These men saw the signs the LORD did in Egypt.
They saw the signs the LORD did in the wilderness.
These men tested the LORD ten times.
They did not listen to the LORD’s voice.
None of these men will see the land.
The LORD promised this land to their fathers.
All who treated the LORD with contempt will not see the land.
passages.original: וְאוּלָ֖ם חַי־ אָ֑נִי וְיִמָּלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־ יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ כִּ֣י כָל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הָרֹאִ֤ים אֶת־ כְּבֹדִי֙ וְאֶת־ אֹ֣תֹתַ֔י אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֥יתִי בְמִצְרַ֖יִם וּבַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּ֣וּ אֹתִ֗י זֶ֚ה עֶ֣שֶׂר פְּעָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי׃ אִם־ יִרְאוּ֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָ֑ם וְכָל־ מְנַאֲצַ֖י לֹ֥א יִרְאֽוּהָ׃

passages.text: But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
passages.sermon:
My servant is Caleb.
Caleb has a different spirit.
Caleb has followed Me with his whole heart.
I will bring Caleb into the land where he has gone.
Caleb’s descendants will inherit that land.
passages.original: וְעַבְדִּ֣י כָלֵ֗ב עֵ֣קֶב הָֽיְתָ֞ה ר֤וּחַ אַחֶ֙רֶת֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיְמַלֵּ֖א אַחֲרָ֑י וַהֲבִֽיאֹתִ֗יו אֶל־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֣א שָׁ֔מָּה וְזַרְע֖וֹ יוֹרִשֶֽׁנָּה׃

passages.text: Now since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.”
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites live in the valley.
The Canaanites also live in the valley.
You must not go into the valley.
Tomorrow, turn back.
Go into the wilderness.
Travel along the road that leads to the Red Sea.
passages.original: וְהָֽעֲמָלֵקִ֥י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בָּעֵ֑מֶק מָחָ֗ר פְּנ֨וּ וּסְע֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר דֶּ֥רֶךְ יַם־ סֽוּף׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD said these words.
The Israelites are a wicked congregation.
They grumble against the LORD.
The LORD asked, “How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me?”
The LORD said, “I have heard the complaints of the Israelites.”
The Israelites complain against the LORD.
The LORD knows their complaints.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃ עַד־ מָתַ֗י לָעֵדָ֤ה הָֽרָעָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥מָּה מַלִּינִ֖ים עָלָ֑י אֶת־ תְּלֻנּ֞וֹת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵ֧מָּה מַלִּינִ֛ים עָלַ֖י שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD said, “Tell the Israelites this.”
The LORD lives forever.
The LORD makes this promise.
The LORD said, “I will do to you what I heard you say.”
The LORD will act according to the words He heard from the Israelites.
passages.original: אֱמֹ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם חַי־ אָ֙נִי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ לֹ֕א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּרְתֶּ֖ם בְּאָזְנָ֑י כֵּ֖ן אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Your bodies will fall in this wilderness—all who were numbered in the census, everyone twenty years of age or older—because you have grumbled against Me.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said, "Your bodies will fall in this wilderness."
This will happen to all who were counted in the census.
This will happen to everyone who is twenty years old or older.
You grumbled against Me.
Because you grumbled, you will die in this wilderness.
passages.original: בַּמִּדְבָּ֣ר הַ֠זֶּה יִפְּל֨וּ פִגְרֵיכֶ֜ם וְכָל־ פְּקֻדֵיכֶם֙ לְכָל־ מִסְפַּרְכֶ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲלִֽינֹתֶ֖ם עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Surely none of you will enter the land in which I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God promised to give them a land.
God swore to settle them in that land.
God said, “None of you will enter that land.”
God made one exception for Caleb son of Jephunneh.
God made another exception for Joshua son of Nun.
Only Caleb and Joshua will enter the land.
passages.original: אִם־ אַתֶּם֙ תָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־ יָדִ֔י לְשַׁכֵּ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּ֑הּ כִּ֚י אִם־ כָּלֵ֣ב בֶּן־ יְפֻנֶּ֔ה וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־ נֽוּן׃

passages.text: But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected—and they will enjoy it.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said, “You claimed your children would become plunder.
You thought harm would come to them.
But I will bring your children into the land.
You rejected this land.
Your children will know the land.
They will enjoy the land you refused.”
passages.original: וְטַ֨פְּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם לָבַ֣ז יִהְיֶ֑ה וְהֵבֵיאתִ֣י אֹתָ֔ם וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְאַסְתֶּ֖ם בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said, “You will not enter the promised land.
You rejected My promise.
You did not trust Me.
Your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
You will die here.
You will not reach the land I promised.”
passages.original: וּפִגְרֵיכֶ֖ם אַתֶּ֑ם יִפְּל֖וּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God said their children would live in the wilderness.
Their children would be shepherds for forty years.
Their children would suffer because of the parents’ unfaithfulness.
Their children would suffer until all the parents’ bodies lay dead in the wilderness.
passages.original: וּ֠בְנֵיכֶם יִהְי֨וּ רֹעִ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְנָשְׂא֖וּ אֶת־ זְנוּתֵיכֶ֑ם עַד־ תֹּ֥ם פִּגְרֵיכֶ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years—a year for each day—and you will experience My alienation.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God had sent them to spy out the land of Canaan.
They explored the land for forty days.
God said each day would count as a year.
The Israelites would bear their guilt for forty years.
They would wander in the wilderness for forty years.
They would experience God’s rejection during this time.
passages.original: בְּמִסְפַּ֨ר הַיָּמִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־ תַּרְתֶּ֣ם אֶת־ הָאָרֶץ֮ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים יוֹם֒ י֣וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֞ה י֣וֹם לַשָּׁנָ֗ה תִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־ עֲוֺנֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ תְּנוּאָתִֽי׃

passages.text: I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.”
passages.sermon:
I am the LORD.
I have spoken.
I will do this to the whole wicked congregation.
This congregation has conspired against Me.
They will come to their end in this wilderness.
They will die there.
passages.original: אֲנִ֣י יְהוָה֮ דִּבַּרְתִּי֒ אִם־ לֹ֣א׀ זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֗ה לְכָל־ הָעֵדָ֤ה הָֽרָעָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את הַנּוֹעָדִ֖ים עָלָ֑י בַּמִּדְבָּ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה יִתַּ֖מּוּ וְשָׁ֥ם יָמֻֽתוּ׃

passages.text: So the men Moses had sent to spy out the land, who had returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing out a bad report about the land— those men who had brought out the bad report about the land—were struck down by a plague before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Moses sent some men to explore the land.
These men returned to the people of Israel.
They made the whole congregation complain against Moses.
They did this by bringing a bad report about the land.
These men spoke evil about the land.
The LORD sent a plague against them.
These men died by the plague before the LORD.
passages.original: וְהָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁלַ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָת֣וּר אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּשֻׁ֗בוּ וַיִּלּוֹנוּ עָלָיו֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה לְהוֹצִ֥יא דִבָּ֖ה עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃ וַיָּמֻ֙תוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים מוֹצִאֵ֥י דִבַּת־ הָאָ֖רֶץ רָעָ֑ה בַּמַּגֵּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Of those men who had gone to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the son of Nun.
Caleb was the son of Jephunneh.
Both men went to spy out the land.
Other men also went to spy out the land.
Only Joshua and Caleb remained alive from those men.
passages.original: וִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־ נ֔וּן וְכָלֵ֖ב בֶּן־ יְפֻנֶּ֑ה חָיוּ֙ מִן־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הַֽהֹלְכִ֖ים לָת֥וּר אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And when Moses relayed these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
God had spoken to Moses.
Moses told all the Israelites what God had said.
The Israelites heard these words.
The people mourned deeply.
They were very sad.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֶֽל־ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֥וּ הָעָ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Early the next morning they got up and went up toward the ridge of the hill country. “We have indeed sinned,” they said, “but we will go to the place the LORD has promised.”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were the people Moses led.
Early the next morning, the Israelites got up.
They went up toward the top of the hill country.
They said, “We have sinned.”
They said, “We will go to the place the LORD has promised.”
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּֽעֲל֥וּ אֶל־ רֹאשׁ־ הָהָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֶּ֗נּוּ וְעָלִ֛ינוּ אֶל־ הַמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה כִּ֥י חָטָֽאנוּ׃

passages.text: But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!
passages.sermon: Moses spoke to the people of Israel.\r\nHe said, "Why are you disobeying the command of the LORD?\r\nYou will not succeed."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֛ה אַתֶּ֥ם עֹבְרִ֖ים אֶת־ פִּ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהִ֖וא לֹ֥א תִצְלָֽח׃

passages.text: Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people of Israel.
He warned them.
He said, “Do not go up the mountain.
The LORD is not with you.
If you go, your enemies will defeat you.”
passages.original: אַֽל־ תַּעֲל֔וּ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין יְהוָ֖ה בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וְלֹא֙ תִּנָּ֣גְפ֔וּ לִפְנֵ֖י אֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: For there the Amalekites and Canaanites will face you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you.”
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites are there in front of you.
The Canaanites are also there in front of you.
They are your enemies.
You will fall by the sword.
You will be defeated in battle.
You have turned away from the LORD.
The LORD will not be with you.
passages.original: כִּי֩ הָעֲמָלֵקִ֨י וְהַכְּנַעֲנִ֥י שָׁם֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם וּנְפַלְתֶּ֖ם בֶּחָ֑רֶב כִּֽי־ עַל־ כֵּ֤ן שַׁבְתֶּם֙ מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But they dared to go up to the ridge of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp.
passages.sermon:
The people tried to go up to the top of the hill country.
Moses stayed in the camp.
The ark of the covenant of the LORD also stayed in the camp.
Moses did not leave the camp.
The ark did not leave the camp.
The people went up without Moses and without the ark.
passages.original: וַיַּעְפִּ֕לוּ לַעֲל֖וֹת אֶל־ רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר וַאֲר֤וֹן בְּרִית־ יְהוָה֙ וּמֹשֶׁ֔ה לֹא־ מָ֖שׁוּ מִקֶּ֥רֶב הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country came down, attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah.
passages.sermon:
The Amalekites lived in the hill country.
The Canaanites also lived in the hill country.
The Amalekites and Canaanites came down from the hill country.
They attacked the Israelites.
They defeated the Israelites.
They chased the Israelites all the way to Hormah.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤רֶד הָעֲמָלֵקִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּהָ֣ר הַה֑וּא וַיַּכּ֥וּם וַֽיַּכְּת֖וּם עַד־ הַֽחָרְמָֽה׃פ
